findings.title: JADEPUFFER: Agentic ransomware for automated database extortion
findings.summary_md: Sysdig Threat Research Team documents what it assesses as the first agentic ransomware operation, driven end to end by an LLM. Entry came through Langflow CVE-2025-3248, an unauthenticated RCE in the /api/v1/validate/code endpoint, after which the agent harvested MinIO and database credentials, took over an Alibaba Nacos server using CVE-2021-29441 and its default JWT signing key, and encrypted 1,342 Nacos configuration items with an ephemeral MySQL AES key that was never persisted, leaving the victim unrecoverable even if they paid. IoCs include C2 45.131.66.106 with a cron beacon to port 4444 every 30 minutes, staging server 64.20.53.230, ransom table README_RANSOM, and a 31-second failure diagnosis and correction cycle cited as evidence of autonomous operation.

findings.title: JADEPUFFER evolves: The agentic threat actor deploys ransomware built to destroy AI models
findings.summary_md: Follow-up Sysdig report shows the same operator returning to the same Langflow instance with ENCFORGE, a UPX 5.20-packed Go 1.22.12 ransomware delivered as lockd, targeting roughly 180 file extensions weighted toward AI and ML artifacts such as .safetensors, .gguf, .ckpt, .faiss, and .parquet. After a failed binary fetch the agent built a working container escape through the Docker socket using privileged host-PID containers and nsenter in 5 minutes 24 seconds, and the report estimates rebuilding a production fine-tuned model costs $75,000 to $500,000. It provides SHA-256 hashes for the packed and unpacked binary, C2 34.153.223.102:9191, campaign task IDs gcp_h1 and gcp_test, and the extortion contact e78393397@proton.me shared with the July 1 report.
